records.source: Παῦλος καὶ Τιμόθεος δοῦλοι Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Φιλίπποις σὺν ἐπισκόποις καὶ διακόνοις·
records.gloss: Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, to all the holy ones in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with overseers and deacons;
pieces: From Paul and Timothy, servants of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, to all God's holy people in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus who live in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons.

L.1: Paul and Timothy, slaves of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, to all the holy ones in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus who are in Philippi, with [the] overseers and deacons.

R.1: This letter is from Paul and Timothy. We are servants who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. We are writing to all of God's holy people in Philippi who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and also to the leaders who watch over the church and those who serve it.

decisions.choice: slaves: people owned by their master and wholly at his service
decisions.reason: δοῦλοι is the ordinary word for a slave, someone who belongs to another, not a hired servant who could leave. Paul and Timothy describe themselves as owned by Christ Jesus. In the Greek Old Testament the same word also gives an honored title to Moses and David as "servants of the Lord" (Joshua 14:7; 2 Samuel 7:5), so it carries both humility and honor. Paul will use it of Christ himself in 2:7.

decisions.choice: people set apart as belonging to God
decisions.reason: ἁγίοις describes every believer, not a select few: the whole church is God's holy people, as Israel was (Exodus 19:6), set apart "in Christ Jesus".

decisions.choice: overseers: the leaders who watched over the church
alternatives: bishops, in the later sense of one bishop over many churches
decisions.reason: ἐπισκόποις means someone who watches over others. The word is plural and the church is one town's church, so it names a group of local leaders; in Acts 20:17 and 20:28 the same people are called elders and overseers. The later pattern of one bishop over a region is not in view.

decisions.choice: a recognized group who served the church alongside the overseers
alternatives: deacons as a later church office
decisions.reason: διακόνοις means one who serves or assists. Named next to the overseers, it refers to a known group in the church (compare 1 Timothy 3:8-13), but the letter does not say what their duties were, and nothing should be read in from later church structures.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Christ Jesus"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT marks a variant in the order of these two names. The meaning does not change, so there is no footnote.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave". Readable keeps the idea of belonging.

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B, R)
decisions.reason: In current English "saints" usually means unusually good people or those honored by a church; Paul is writing to the whole congregation.

decisions.choice: those who serve the church
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word means rather than using a church title.

decisions.choice: who belong to Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: "In Christ" means being united with him; Readable says so plainly.

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: Grace to you and peace from God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ.
pieces: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.2: I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will show you grace and give you peace.

decisions.choice: one source: God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ together
decisions.reason: A single ἀπὸ ("from") governs both names, so Jesus is named with God the Father as the one source of grace and peace. Paul opens almost every letter this way (Romans 1:7; 1 Corinthians 1:3).

decisions.choice: a greeting turned into a blessing
decisions.reason: Greek letters normally opened with a one-word "greetings". Paul replaces it with χάρις (grace), a word close to it in sound, and adds εἰρήνη (peace), the usual Jewish greeting. It is a wish and a prayer for God's favor and wholeness.

decisions.choice: Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: I pray that ... will show you grace and give you peace
decisions.reason: The greeting has no verb. Readable states it as the prayer it is, so young readers do not read it as a heading.

records.source: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ μνείᾳ ὑμῶν πάντοτε ἐν πάσῃ δεήσει μου ὑπὲρ πάντων ὑμῶν, μετὰ χαρᾶς τὴν δέησιν ποιούμενος, ἐπὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἀπὸ τῆς πρώτης ἡμέρας ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν, πεποιθὼς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ὅτι ὁ ἐναρξάμενος ἐν ὑμῖν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐπιτελέσει ἄχρι ἡμέρας Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ· καθώς ἐστιν δίκαιον ἐμοὶ τοῦτο φρονεῖν ὑπὲρ πάντων ὑμῶν, διὰ τὸ ἔχειν με ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμᾶς, ἔν τε τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀπολογίᾳ καὶ βεβαιώσει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου συγκοινωνούς μου τῆς χάριτος πάντας ὑμᾶς ὄντας·
records.gloss: I thank the God of me upon every the remembrance of you, \v 4 always in every prayer of me for all of you, with joy the prayer making, \v 5 for the partnership of you in the gospel from the first day until the now, \v 6 having been persuaded of this very thing, that the [one] having begun in you a work good will complete [it] until [the] day of Christ Jesus; \v 7 just as it is right for me this to think on behalf of all of you, because of the to have me in the heart you, both in the chains of me and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, fellow sharers of me of the grace all you being.
pieces: Each time I remember you, I give thanks to my God.
In every prayer I offer for all of you, I always pray with joy,
because from the very first day until now you have been partners with me in the gospel.
Of this I am convinced: the one who started a good work in you will keep working at it until it is finished on the day of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

It is only right for me to think this way about all of you, because I hold you in my heart. All of you are partners with me in God's grace, both in my chains and as I defend the gospel and show that it stands firm.

L.3: I thank my God at every remembrance of you,
L.4: always in every prayer of mine for all of you, making the prayer with joy,
L.5: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now,
L.6: being persuaded of this very thing, that the [one] who began a good work in you will complete [it] until [the] day of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus;
L.7: just as it is right for me to think this about all of you, because I have you in [my] heart, since both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel all of you are fellow sharers with me of the grace.

R.3: Every time I think of you, I thank my God.
R.4: And whenever I pray for all of you, I pray with joy,
R.5: because you have worked with me to spread the good news, from the first day you believed until now.
R.6: I am sure of this: God began a good work in you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will keep at it until it is complete on the day {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus comes back.
R.7: It is right that I think of all of you like this, because you have a place in my heart. All of you share God's grace with me, both while I am a prisoner and while I defend the good news and show that it is true.

decisions.choice: verses 3-7 are one sentence
alternatives: verse 7 begins a new sentence, as the SBLGNT's raised dot allows
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot at the end of verse 6, but verse 7 opens with καθώς ("just as") and gives the ground for the confidence of verse 6, so it cannot stand on its own. The record keeps verses 3-7 together; the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: every time Paul remembers them
alternatives: for every remembrance of me you have shown (for example, your gifts)
decisions.reason: μνείᾳ with ὑμῶν could mean the Philippians' remembering of Paul, which would fit their gifts in 4:10-18. But in Paul's prayer reports the same kind of phrase means his remembering of others (Romans 1:9; 1 Thessalonians 1:2), and verse 4 goes on to his own prayers.

decisions.choice: active partnership in the work of the gospel
decisions.reason: κοινωνίᾳ means having a share in something together. With εἰς ("for, toward") the gospel it is a shared work: the Philippians took part in Paul's mission with prayer, people and money (4:14-16). Verse 7 picks the idea up again with "fellow sharers".

decisions.choice: from the day the church at Philippi began
decisions.reason: Acts 16:12-40 tells how Paul first preached at Philippi and how Lydia and the jailer's family believed. Philippians 4:15 says they shared in his work from that first time on.

decisions.choice: God, who began his saving work in them, will finish it
decisions.reason: The one who began is not named, but only God can be meant (compare 2:13). The "good work" is his work in them, which includes their partnership in verse 5 but is wider: Paul is sure God will not leave it half done. ὑμῖν is plural and may also mean "among you".

decisions.choice: the day Christ returns as judge and savior
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of "the day of the Lord" (Amos 5:18; Joel 2:31). Paul applies it to Christ Jesus, whose coming he awaits (1:10; 2:16; 3:20).

decisions.choice: to think and feel this way: a settled attitude
decisions.reason: φρονέω is a key word of the letter (2:2, 2:5, 4:2): a whole way of thinking that includes affection.

decisions.choice: Paul holds the Philippians in his heart
alternatives: the Philippians hold Paul in their heart
decisions.reason: The Greek has two accusatives with the infinitive, με (me) and ὑμᾶς (you), and either can be the subject: "because I have you in my heart" or "because you have me in your heart". We read με as the subject because it stands first and because verse 8 goes on to Paul's own longing for them. The other reading fits their loyalty to him and is fully possible.

decisions.choice: legal words: defending the gospel in court and confirming it
decisions.reason: ἀπολογίᾳ is a defense speech before a judge, and βεβαιώσει the legal confirming of something as valid. Paul is awaiting trial (1:13, 1:16), and he treats his case as the gospel's case.

decisions.choice: a share with Paul in God's grace, including the grace to suffer
alternatives: a share in the privilege of Paul's ministry
decisions.reason: The article points to a particular grace: God's favor that called Paul to his work and keeps him in it, chains and all. In 1:29 suffering for Christ is called something "granted" by grace.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: partners with me (B); worked with me (R)
decisions.reason: The partnership is with Paul, as 4:15 says ("shared with me") and as verse 7 makes explicit; Balanced and Readable name him. Balanced also echoes the word in verse 7 ("partners with me in God's grace").

decisions.choice: the first day you believed; God ... {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; the day Christ Jesus comes back
decisions.reason: Readable names what the Greek implies: the day they first believed, God as the one at work, and the day of Christ's return.

decisions.choice: while I am a prisoner
decisions.reason: Paul's chains stand for his imprisonment; Readable says so.

records.heading: Thanks and prayer

records.source: μάρτυς γάρ μου ὁ θεός, ὡς ἐπιποθῶ πάντας ὑμᾶς ἐν σπλάγχνοις Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: Witness for of me [is] the God, how I long for all you in [the] inner parts of Christ Jesus.
pieces: God is my witness how much I long for every one of you with the deep love of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

L.8: For God [is] my witness, how I long for all of you in [the] tender affection of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.

R.8: God knows how much I long to see all of you. I love you with the tender love of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

decisions.choice: a solemn oath: God can confirm it
alternatives: a general remark that God sees everything
decisions.reason: Paul calls God as witness when he wants to assure readers he is telling the truth about something they cannot see, such as his prayers or his feelings (Romans 1:9; 1 Thessalonians 2:5).

decisions.choice: deep affection, felt in the inner being
decisions.reason: σπλάγχνοις literally means the inner organs, which Greek speakers treated as the seat of strong feeling, much as we speak of the heart.

decisions.choice: Christ's own affection, at work in Paul
decisions.reason: Paul does not love them merely with his own feelings: the tender love of Christ Jesus moves in him (compare Galatians 2:20).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: God knows how much ...; long to see
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the oath in plain words, and says what the longing is for: to be with them again (compare 2:26 and 4:1).

records.source: καὶ τοῦτο προσεύχομαι ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ὑμῶν ἔτι μᾶλλον καὶ μᾶλλον περισσεύῃ ἐν ἐπιγνώσει καὶ πάσῃ αἰσθήσει, εἰς τὸ δοκιμάζειν ὑμᾶς τὰ διαφέροντα, ἵνα ἦτε εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀπρόσκοποι εἰς ἡμέραν Χριστοῦ, πεπληρωμένοι καρπὸν δικαιοσύνης τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς δόξαν καὶ ἔπαινον θεοῦ.
records.gloss: And this I pray, that the love of you yet more and more may abound in knowledge and all discernment, \v 10 for the to test you the things excelling, so that you may be pure and without stumbling for [the] day of Christ, \v 11 having been filled [with the] fruit of righteousness, the [one] through Jesus Christ, to glory and praise of God.
pieces: And this is what I pray: that your love will overflow more and more, with full knowledge and every kind of insight,
so that you can test and recognize what really matters. Then on the day of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} you will be pure and free from stumbling,
full of the fruit of righteousness that is produced through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so that God receives glory and praise.

L.9: And this I pray, that your love may overflow yet more and more in full knowledge and every [kind of] insight,
L.10: so that you test and approve the things that matter, so that you may be pure and without stumbling for [the] day of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.11: filled with [the] fruit of righteousness which [is] through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, to [the] glory and praise of God.

R.9: Here is what I pray for you. I pray that your love will keep growing more and more, along with real knowledge and good sense.
R.10: Then you will be able to see what is truly best. You will be pure, and nothing will make you fall, when {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} comes back.
R.11: Your lives will be full of the fruit of a righteous life, which Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} produces in you. All this will bring glory and praise to God.

decisions.choice: full knowledge and moral insight
decisions.reason: ἐπιγνώσει is real, growing knowledge, especially of God and his will (Colossians 1:9). αἰσθήσει occurs only here in the New Testament: the practical sense to tell good from bad in a given situation. Paul wants their love to grow together with both.

decisions.choice: to test and so to recognize what really matters
alternatives: to tell apart things that differ
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζειν means to test and then approve; διαφέροντα can mean "things that differ" or "things that excel". The phrase means the ability to sort out what is best, as in Romans 2:18.

decisions.choice: pure, and not stumbling
alternatives: sincere, and giving no offense to others
decisions.reason: εἰλικρινεῖς means unmixed, without hidden motives. ἀπρόσκοποι can mean "not stumbling" or "not causing others to stumble" (1 Corinthians 10:32). Standing before Christ on his day, the first sense, blameless, fits best.

decisions.choice: the day of Christ's return
decisions.reason: As in verse 6: the day of the Lord, now the day of Christ (2:16).

decisions.choice: the harvest of right living that Jesus Christ produces
alternatives: the reward that comes from being declared right with God
decisions.reason: "Fruit of righteousness" is an Old Testament phrase for upright conduct (Proverbs 11:30; Amos 6:12; compare James 3:18). Here it grows "through Jesus Christ": not their own achievement, but what he produces in those he has made right with God (3:9).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the singular "fruit"
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts have the plural. The singular is the better-attested reading and the meaning hardly changes.

decisions.choice: the final goal: God's glory and praise
decisions.reason: The whole prayer ends with God receiving glory and praise, as the hymn in 2:11 does.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} / Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the sentence broken into three (B) or four (R)
decisions.reason: Verses 9-11 are one Greek sentence; Balanced and Readable break it where each clause can stand, keeping its order.

decisions.choice: the fruit of a righteous life
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the fruit is right living (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: when Christ comes back
decisions.reason: Readable names the event the day refers to.

records.source: Γινώσκειν δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι τὰ κατ’ ἐμὲ μᾶλλον εἰς προκοπὴν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐλήλυθεν, ὥστε τοὺς δεσμούς μου φανεροὺς ἐν Χριστῷ γενέσθαι ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ πραιτωρίῳ καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς πᾶσιν, καὶ τοὺς πλείονας τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἐν κυρίῳ πεποιθότας τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου περισσοτέρως τολμᾶν ἀφόβως τὸν λόγον λαλεῖν.
records.gloss: Now to know you I want, brothers, that the things concerning me rather to [the] advance of the gospel have come, \v 13 so that the chains of me clearly known in Christ to become in the whole praetorium and to the rest all, \v 14 and the most of the brothers in [the] Lord having been persuaded by the chains of me more abundantly to dare fearlessly the word to speak.
pieces: I want you to understand, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that what has happened to me has moved the gospel forward rather than holding it back.
As a result, the whole imperial guard and everyone else here have come to see that I am in chains for the sake of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
And my chains have given most of the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} confidence in the Lord, so that they dare to speak the word far more boldly and without fear.

L.12: Now I want you to know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that the things concerning me have rather come to [the] advance of the gospel,
L.13: so that my chains have become clearly known [as being] in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} in the whole praetorian guard and to all the rest,
L.14: and most of the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, having become confident in [the] Lord by my chains, dare far more to speak the word without fear.

R.12: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I want you to know that the things that have happened to me have helped the good news spread even more.
R.13: All the soldiers of the emperor's guard, and everyone else here, now know that I am a prisoner because I serve {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
R.14: And because I am in chains, most of the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} here trust the Lord more. Now they are much braver about telling God's message, and they are not afraid.

decisions.choice: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοί addresses the whole church, which includes women such as Lydia (Acts 16:14-15) and Euodia and Syntyche (4:2). The believers in verse 14 are likewise the church at large.

decisions.choice: contrary to what they might fear, his situation has helped
decisions.reason: μᾶλλον here means "rather, instead": the Philippians would expect Paul's arrest to hold the gospel back, but it has moved it forward. προκοπὴν is progress, a pioneer's advance; Paul uses it again of the Philippians' own progress in 1:25.

decisions.choice: the imperial guard: the soldiers who guarded Paul
decisions.reason: πραιτωρίῳ can mean a body of troops, the Praetorian Guard in Rome, or a governor's residence, as in Mark 15:16 and Acts 23:35. "And to all the rest" points to people, which favors the guard. Where Paul was held (Rome, or possibly Ephesus or Caesarea) is not stated in the letter; 4:22 mentions "Caesar's household".

decisions.choice: it has become clear that his chains are for Christ
decisions.reason: ἐν Χριστῷ goes with "clearly known": people now see that Paul is a prisoner because of Christ, not for a crime.

decisions.choice: made confident in the Lord by Paul's chains
alternatives: "brothers in the Lord" as one phrase
decisions.reason: "In the Lord" could go with "brothers", but believers are always brothers in the Lord, so it more likely says where their new confidence rests.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the word"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, some of them early, add "of God", and a few "of the Lord". The SBLGNT prints the shorter reading. The meaning is the same: the message about Christ.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul is addressing the whole church, women and men, so the inclusive default spells that out. Traditional is one tap away.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: praetorian guard (L); imperial guard (B)
decisions.reason: "Praetorium" is not English; the guard is the reading chosen (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: because I serve Christ; God's message
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "in Christ" means for the chains, and what "the word" is.

records.heading: Paul's chains move the gospel forward

records.source: Τινὲς μὲν καὶ διὰ φθόνον καὶ ἔριν, τινὲς δὲ καὶ δι’ εὐδοκίαν τὸν Χριστὸν κηρύσσουσιν·
records.gloss: Some indeed even because of envy and strife, but some also because of goodwill the Christ are proclaiming;
pieces: Some, to be sure, are proclaiming {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} from jealousy and a spirit of rivalry; others do it from goodwill.

L.15: Some indeed proclaim the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} even from envy and rivalry, but some also from goodwill.

R.15: Some people are telling others about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} because they are jealous of me and want to compete with me. But others do it because they want to help.

decisions.choice: Christian preachers where Paul was held, with mixed motives
decisions.reason: These people preach the true Christ, which is why Paul can rejoice in verse 18. Contrast 3:2, where he warns against teachers whose message is wrong.

decisions.choice: envy and rivalry, aimed at Paul
decisions.reason: φθόνον is jealousy and ἔριν is quarrelsome rivalry. Verse 17 shows Paul is their target: they want to add to his troubles.

decisions.choice: goodwill toward Paul
decisions.reason: εὐδοκίαν can describe God's good pleasure (2:13), but here it is the preachers' motive, the opposite of envy: they wish Paul well.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. The Greek has the article here, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: jealous of me; want to help
decisions.reason: Readable names the person the envy and goodwill are aimed at, as verses 16-17 do.

records.source: οἱ μὲν ἐξ ἀγάπης, εἰδότες ὅτι εἰς ἀπολογίαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου κεῖμαι, οἱ δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας τὸν Χριστὸν καταγγέλλουσιν, οὐχ ἁγνῶς, οἰόμενοι θλῖψιν ἐγείρειν τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου.
records.gloss: the ones indeed out of love, knowing that for [the] defense of the gospel I am set, \v 17 but the ones out of selfish ambition the Christ are proclaiming, not purely, supposing affliction to raise to the chains of me.
pieces: These act out of love, because they know I am stationed here to defend the gospel.
The others proclaim {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} out of selfish ambition, with motives that are not pure. They think they can make my time in chains more painful.

L.16: The ones [do so] out of love, knowing that I am set here for [the] defense of the gospel;
L.17: but the others proclaim the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} out of selfish ambition, not purely, supposing [they can] raise up affliction for my chains.

R.16: The ones who preach out of love know that God has put me here to defend the good news.
R.17: But the others tell about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} because they want to get ahead themselves. Their reasons are not pure. They think they can make things harder for me while I am in prison.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the order of verses 16 and 17
alternatives: the two verses in reverse order
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts put verse 17 before verse 16, so that the order matches verse 15 (envy first, goodwill second). The earliest manuscripts have the order printed here, where Paul turns the pattern around.

decisions.choice: placed here, appointed for the defense of the gospel
decisions.reason: κεῖμαι means to lie or be set somewhere; with "for" it means to be appointed for a task, as in 1 Thessalonians 3:3. Paul's imprisonment is part of his calling, not a setback.

decisions.choice: selfish ambition, a party spirit
decisions.reason: ἐριθείας is self-seeking rivalry, the attitude that builds a faction. Paul warns the Philippians against it in 2:3.

decisions.choice: with impure motives, intending to make his imprisonment harder
decisions.reason: ἁγνῶς ("purely") is negated: they preach the right message from the wrong motives. οἰόμενοι ("supposing") hints that their plan does not work: Paul rejoices anyway.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: God has put me here
decisions.reason: The Greek does not name who appointed Paul, but it can only be God; Readable says so.

pieces: What does it matter?

decisions.choice: a rhetorical question: what does it matter?
decisions.reason: τί γάρ is a short way of saying "so what follows from that?" Paul answers it at once.

decisions.choice: What does it matter? (B); does that really matter? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

records.source: πλὴν ὅτι παντὶ τρόπῳ, εἴτε προφάσει εἴτε ἀληθείᾳ, Χριστὸς καταγγέλλεται, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ χαίρω· ἀλλὰ καὶ χαρήσομαι, οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι τοῦτό μοι ἀποβήσεται εἰς σωτηρίαν διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν δεήσεως καὶ ἐπιχορηγίας τοῦ πνεύματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, κατὰ τὴν ἀποκαραδοκίαν καὶ ἐλπίδα μου ὅτι ἐν οὐδενὶ αἰσχυνθήσομαι, ἀλλ’ ἐν πάσῃ παρρησίᾳ ὡς πάντοτε καὶ νῦν μεγαλυνθήσεται Χριστὸς ἐν τῷ σώματί μου, εἴτε διὰ ζωῆς εἴτε διὰ θανάτου.
records.gloss: Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice; yes, and I will rejoice, \v 19 for I know that this for me will turn out to salvation through the of you prayer and supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, \v 20 according to the eager expectation and hope of me that in nothing I will be put to shame, but in all boldness as always also now Christ will be magnified in the body of me, whether through life or through death.
pieces: All that matters is that in every way, whether as a pretext or in truth, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is being proclaimed, and in that I rejoice. Yes, and I will go on rejoicing,
for I know that through your prayers and the help supplied by the Spirit of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, this will turn out for my salvation.

I eagerly expect and hope that I will not be put to shame in anything. Instead, with all boldness, now as always, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will be shown to be great in my body, whether through my life or through my death.

L.18: Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will rejoice,
L.19: for I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your prayer and [the] supply of the Spirit of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.20: according to my eager expectation and hope that I will be put to shame in nothing, but [that] with all boldness, as always, so now also {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.

R.18: But what matters is this: one way or another, people are telling about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, whether their reasons are false or true. That makes me full of joy. And I will keep on being full of joy,
R.19: because I know that all this will lead to my salvation. You are praying for me, and the Spirit of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is helping me.
R.20: I am eagerly expecting and hoping that I will never fail and be put to shame. I hope to be very brave, so that now, as always, people will see how great {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is by what happens to my body, whether I live or die.

decisions.choice: whether as a cover for other motives or sincerely
alternatives: whether false doctrine or true doctrine
decisions.reason: προφάσει is a pretext, a show put on to hide the real aim; ἀληθείᾳ (truth) is here its opposite, sincerity. The message is the same either way; only the motives differ.

decisions.choice: only this matters: Christ is proclaimed
decisions.reason: πλὴν ὅτι introduces the one thing that counts against all the rest.

decisions.choice: the words of Job 13:16 in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: "This will turn out for my salvation" repeats word for word what Job says in the Greek Old Testament, when he trusts that God will vindicate him in spite of what others think. Paul, like Job, expects God to prove him in the right.

decisions.choice: salvation: final vindication before God, whether Paul lives or dies
decisions.reason: σωτηρίαν can mean rescue from danger or salvation in the full sense. Verse 20 says Christ will be honored "whether by life or by death", so Paul is not only counting on release; the echo of Job also points to being vindicated before God. But in verse 25 he does expect to live, and release may be part of what he means.

decisions.choice: the Philippians' prayer and the help the Spirit supplies, together
decisions.reason: One article (τῆς) governs both nouns: as they pray, the Spirit's help is given. ἐπιχορηγίας is a generous supply; the Spirit may be what is supplied or the one who supplies, and the sense is the same. "The Spirit of Jesus Christ" is the Holy Spirit (Romans 8:9; Galatians 4:6).

decisions.choice: eager expectation and hope
decisions.reason: ἀποκαραδοκίαν pictures someone straining forward to see what is coming (it is used of creation in Romans 8:19). Hope in the Bible is confident expectation, not wishful thinking.

decisions.choice: put to shame: let down when it counts
decisions.reason: In the Psalms those who trust God "will not be put to shame" (Psalm 25:2-3; Isaiah 49:23): their trust will not be disappointed in public. Paul means the same.

decisions.choice: Christ will be shown to be great
decisions.reason: μεγαλυνθήσεται means to make great in the eyes of others, to honor. Nothing can add to Christ; what happens to Paul's body will show how great he is.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the sentence broken into several
decisions.reason: Verses 18-20 run on in Greek; Balanced and Readable divide them at the natural joins.

decisions.choice: full of joy
decisions.reason: As in 4:4, "rejoice" is mostly church language; Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: I hope to be very brave
decisions.reason: The Greek attaches boldness to the clause about Christ being honored; Readable gives the boldness to Paul, whose courage is meant.

records.source: ἐμοὶ γὰρ τὸ ζῆν Χριστὸς καὶ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν κέρδος.
records.gloss: To me for the to live [is] Christ and the to die [is] gain.
pieces: For me, living is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and dying is gain.

L.21: For to me, to live [is] {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and to die [is] gain.

R.21: For me, life is all about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. And dying would only be gain for me, since I would be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: living is Christ: Christ is the whole content and aim of life
decisions.reason: The infinitive with the article (τὸ ζῆν) is the subject and Χριστὸς the predicate. Paul does not say his life is useful to Christ; he says that life, for him, means Christ: knowing him, serving him, being united with him (compare 3:8-10; Galatians 2:20).

decisions.choice: gain, profit
decisions.reason: κέρδος is a business word for profit. It returns in 3:7, where Paul counts his former gains as loss. Death is gain because it brings him to Christ (verse 23), not because life is a burden.

decisions.choice: the reason for verse 20
decisions.reason: γὰρ ("for") explains why Paul can face life or death without shame.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: since I would be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Readable adds the reason, which Paul gives himself two verses later (verse 23).

records.source: εἰ δὲ τὸ ζῆν ἐν σαρκί, τοῦτό μοι καρπὸς ἔργου καὶ τί αἱρήσομαι οὐ γνωρίζω·
records.gloss: But if the to live in flesh, this for me [is] fruit of work; and what I will choose I do not make known.
pieces: But if my life in the body continues, that means fruit from my work. So which would I choose? I cannot say.

L.22: But if [I am] to live in the flesh, this [means] fruit of work for me; and what I will choose I do not make known.

R.22: But if I stay alive here on earth, I can keep doing work that brings good results. So I really can't say which I would choose.

decisions.choice: if living on in the body means fruitful work
alternatives: if I live on, that is the fruit of my work
decisions.reason: The Greek is broken off (the SBLGNT marks the break with a dash) and has no verb in the "if" clause. The natural sense is: if staying alive is what lies ahead, that means more fruitful work for Paul.

decisions.choice: life in the body, in this world
decisions.reason: σαρκί ("flesh") here means ordinary bodily life, as in verse 24, not the sinful nature Paul speaks of in 3:3-4.

decisions.choice: I cannot say
decisions.reason: γνωρίζω elsewhere in Paul means "make known, declare" (as in 4:6), not "know". Paul is not confused; he will not state a choice, because the matter is in God's hands.

decisions.choice: here on earth
decisions.reason: Readable avoids "flesh", which young readers may take as skin and muscle.

records.source: συνέχομαι δὲ ἐκ τῶν δύο, τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν ἔχων εἰς τὸ ἀναλῦσαι καὶ σὺν Χριστῷ εἶναι, πολλῷ γὰρ μᾶλλον κρεῖσσον, τὸ δὲ ἐπιμένειν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ἀναγκαιότερον δι’ ὑμᾶς.
records.gloss: But I am hemmed in from the two, the desire having for the to depart and with Christ to be, for [it is] by much more better; \v 24 but the to remain in the flesh [is] more necessary because of you.
pieces: I am pulled in two directions. My desire is to leave this life and be with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, for that is far, far better.
But for your sake it is more needful that I stay on in the body.

L.23: But I am hard pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and to be with {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, for [that is] very much better;
L.24: but to remain in the flesh [is] more necessary for your sake.

R.23: I feel pulled two ways. I want to leave this life and go to be with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. That would be much, much better.
R.24: But you need me, so it is more important that I stay alive.

decisions.choice: hemmed in from both sides
decisions.reason: συνέχομαι means pressed or held in on all sides. Paul feels pulled equally by both choices.

decisions.choice: to depart: to leave this life
decisions.reason: ἀναλῦσαι is used of a ship casting off or soldiers striking camp. Paul uses a gentle word for dying (compare 2 Timothy 4:6).

decisions.choice: departing and being with Christ are one event
alternatives: being with Christ only at the resurrection
decisions.reason: One article governs both infinitives: for Paul, to die is to be with Christ (compare 2 Corinthians 5:8). He does not say more here about what that state is like; elsewhere he waits for the resurrection of the body (3:20-21).

decisions.choice: far, far better
decisions.reason: Paul piles up three comparatives ("by much more better") to say how much better it is.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT marks two small variants: some manuscripts lack "for" in verse 23 and "in" in verse 24. The meaning does not change, so there is no footnote.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: stay alive
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what remaining in the body means.

records.source: καὶ τοῦτο πεποιθὼς οἶδα ὅτι μενῶ καὶ παραμενῶ πᾶσιν ὑμῖν εἰς τὴν ὑμῶν προκοπὴν καὶ χαρὰν τῆς πίστεως, ἵνα τὸ καύχημα ὑμῶν περισσεύῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ διὰ τῆς ἐμῆς παρουσίας πάλιν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
records.gloss: And this having been persuaded of, I know that I will remain and remain alongside all you for the of you progress and joy of the faith, \v 26 so that the boasting of you may abound in Christ Jesus in me through the my coming again to you.
pieces: Since I am sure of this, I know that I will stay, and stay on with all of you, to help you move forward and find joy in the faith.
Then, when I come back to you, you will have even more reason to boast in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus because of me.

L.25: And being persuaded of this, I know that I will remain and remain alongside all of you, for your progress and joy of the faith,
L.26: so that your boasting may abound in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus in me, through my coming to you again.

R.25: Because I am sure of this, I know I will stay alive. I will stay with all of you to help you grow in your faith and have joy in it.
R.26: Then, when I come back to you, you will have even more reason to praise {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus because of me.

decisions.choice: convinced of this: that his staying is needed
alternatives: a revelation that he will live
decisions.reason: "This" points back to verse 24. Paul's confidence rests on what the church needs; it is a settled conviction, not a prophecy (in 2:17 he still speaks of possibly being poured out).

decisions.choice: remain, and remain at their side
decisions.reason: μενῶ and παραμενῶ are a play on words: to stay alive, and to stay beside them to help. The SBLGNT marks a variant with a compound form of the second verb; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: their progress and joy in the faith
alternatives: progress in the faith, and joy in general
decisions.reason: One article joins "progress" and "joy": both belong to their faith. προκοπὴν is the word used of the gospel's advance in verse 12.

decisions.choice: a proud and joyful confidence in what Christ has done
decisions.reason: καύχημα is the ground of boasting. Paul uses it in a good sense when the boast is in Christ (3:3; 2:16). Here Paul's return will give them more reason for it.

decisions.choice: Paul's coming, his presence with them again
decisions.reason: παρουσίας is often used of Christ's coming (1 Thessalonians 4:15), but here "my" makes it Paul's own arrival.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: even more reason to praise
decisions.reason: In everyday English "boast" sounds like showing off. Readable uses "praise", which keeps the joy and the pride in Christ without the bad sense.

records.source: Μόνον ἀξίως τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ Χριστοῦ πολιτεύεσθε, ἵνα εἴτε ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ὑμᾶς εἴτε ἀπὼν ἀκούω τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν, ὅτι στήκετε ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι, μιᾷ ψυχῇ συναθλοῦντες τῇ πίστει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, καὶ μὴ πτυρόμενοι ἐν μηδενὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀντικειμένων ἥτις ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς ἔνδειξις ἀπωλείας, ὑμῶν δὲ σωτηρίας, καὶ τοῦτο ἀπὸ θεοῦ, ὅτι ὑμῖν ἐχαρίσθη τὸ ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, οὐ μόνον τὸ εἰς αὐτὸν πιστεύειν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πάσχειν, τὸν αὐτὸν ἀγῶνα ἔχοντες οἷον εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοὶ καὶ νῦν ἀκούετε ἐν ἐμοί.
records.gloss: Only worthily of the gospel of the Christ live as citizens, so that whether having come and having seen you or being absent I hear the things concerning you, that you are standing firm in one spirit, with one soul contending together for the faith of the gospel, \v 28 and not being frightened in nothing by those opposing, which is to them a sign of destruction, of you but of salvation, and this from God; \v 29 because to you it was granted, the on behalf of Christ, not only the in him to believe but also the on behalf of him to suffer, \v 30 the same contest having such as you saw in me and now hear in me.
pieces: Just one thing: live as citizens in a way worthy of the gospel of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Then, whether I come and see you or am away and only hear about you, I will know that you are standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side as one for the faith of the gospel,
and not letting your opponents frighten you in any way. This courage is a sign to them of their destruction, but of your salvation, and it comes from God.
For God has given you the gift, for the sake of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, not only of believing in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} but also of suffering for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
You are in the same contest that you once watched me face, and that you now hear I am facing still.

L.27: Only live as citizens worthily of the gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear the things concerning you: that you are standing firm in one spirit, with one soul contending side by side for the faith of the gospel,
L.28: and not being frightened in anything by those who oppose [you]; which is for them a sign of destruction, but of your salvation, and this [is] from God;
L.29: because to you it was granted, on behalf of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, not only to believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} but also to suffer on behalf of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.30: having the same contest that you saw in me and now hear [to be] in me.

R.27: Above everything else, live as citizens in a way that matches the good news about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you from far away, I will know that you are standing strong together, one in spirit. I will know that you are working hard side by side, like one person, for the faith that the good news brings.
R.28: And I will know that you are not frightened at all by the people who are against you. This shows them that they will be destroyed, but that you will be saved. And it is God who is doing this.
R.29: God has given you a gift for the sake of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}: not only to believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but also to suffer for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.30: You are in the same fight that you saw me fighting when I was with you, and you hear that I am still fighting it now.

decisions.choice: live as citizens, in the way citizens of the gospel should
decisions.reason: πολιτεύεσθε means to live as a citizen, to take part in the life of a city. Philippi was a Roman colony whose people were proud of their Roman citizenship (Acts 16:12, 16:21, 16:37-38). Paul uses the political word on purpose; in 3:20 he says "our citizenship is in heaven".

decisions.choice: one thing above all
decisions.reason: Μόνον singles out what matters most whatever happens to Paul.

decisions.choice: one spirit: a shared purpose and resolve
alternatives: one Spirit: the Holy Spirit who unites them
decisions.reason: Whether to write "spirit" or "Spirit" is a decision about meaning. πνεύματι is paired with "one soul" (one mind), which suggests the unity of their own spirit. But Paul does speak of "one Spirit" uniting believers (1 Corinthians 12:13; Ephesians 4:4), and in 2:1 he mentions "fellowship of the Spirit", so the Holy Spirit may be meant, and the two senses are close: the Spirit makes them one in spirit.

decisions.choice: striving side by side, as one person, for the faith the gospel brings
alternatives: striving together with the faith, as a team-mate
decisions.reason: συναθλοῦντες is a word from the games: athletes or soldiers fighting side by side (see 4:3). "With one soul" means acting as one. The faith of the gospel is the faith the gospel calls for and proclaims; they strive for its sake.

decisions.choice: startled, intimidated
decisions.reason: πτυρόμενοι is used of a horse shying in fright; it occurs only here in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: their fearless stand is a sign: of destruction to the opponents, of salvation for the believers, and it is God's doing
alternatives: the opponents' hostility is the sign
decisions.reason: ἥτις refers to the whole picture just described, the church standing firm without fear. It points to the opponents' ἀπωλείας (ruin; compare 3:19) and to the believers' salvation. "And this from God" says that the salvation, and the sign of it, come from God.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "of your salvation"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "to you" for "your". The sense is the same, so there is no footnote.

decisions.choice: granted as a gift of grace
decisions.reason: ἐχαρίσθη is related to the word for grace: to give freely as a favor. Suffering for Christ, like believing in him, is a gift God gives, because it unites them with Christ (3:10).

decisions.choice: the same contest they had watched Paul fight at Philippi
decisions.reason: ἀγῶνα is a contest or struggle. The Philippians saw Paul beaten and jailed in their city (Acts 16:19-40; 1 Thessalonians 2:2), and now they hear of his imprisonment.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} / {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: The pronouns refer to Christ.

decisions.choice: the sentence broken into several
decisions.reason: Verses 27-30 are one Greek sentence; Balanced and Readable break it at each new clause.

decisions.choice: This courage (B); God has given (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced names what "which" refers to, and both levels name God as the giver, as "this from God" in verse 28 does.

decisions.choice: when I was with you
decisions.reason: Readable names the time they saw Paul's struggle: his first visit (Acts 16).
